"Oficina do Diabo" marks the first foray into fiction by Brasil Paralelo, a studio renowned for its high-quality documentaries. This stunning film is a masterpiece that showcases the beauty of southern Brazil through breathtaking cinematography, a grandiose soundtrack, and a spectacular screenplay.

The story delves deep into complex and universal themes such as faith, character, vanity, love, and forgiveness, all set against the backdrop of a spiritual battle between good and evil. The narrative is as profound as it is gripping, offering a thought-provoking exploration of the human soul and its struggles.

Roberto Mallet delivers an absolutely fantastic performance, bringing incredible depth and authenticity to his character. His portrayal is a standout in a film filled with stellar moments.

Bravo to the BP studio for this incredible achievement!

A film that is sure to resonate with audiences long after the credits roll.

The best national film (Brazil) I've ever seen and, perhaps, the best film I've ever seen in my life.

The film kept my attention for every second it ran and it still caused me deep reflections.

The settings, the characters, the plot were all very well designed and acted.

Various emotions were also experienced, from laughter to crying.

Whenever I watch a film I hope to receive a message from it, something that makes me reflect and experience the magic of cinema. Well, this film gave me a feeling that I haven't found in cinema for a long time.

Without a doubt, the time I took to watch it was a great investment in my life.

This is the most beautiful Brazilian film ever made. The story is based on the most important spiritual battle we fight, the battle between good and evil in our daily lives. God has a plan for you, just like the Devil. What plan do you want to follow? The film raises these questions in such a wonderful and perfect way. We can all put ourselves in Natan's perspective. The narratives and dialogues are constructed to express the struggle that this battle is. Not to mention the symbolic details that are presented in the film, such as the Eucharist scene. It is not possible to find anything in Brazilian filmography that compares to the photography of this film or the importance of the theme. An unmissable film that should be in the Top 5 of the best Brazilian films of all time.

I just didn't rate it 10/10 due to some weak performances, but that doesn't detract from the film, considering it was produced by an independent producer with budget limitations. Speaking of performances, I positively highlight the most famous actress in the cast, Elisângela, who plays Maria, the protagonist's mother. Her work was linear, as expected from a competent and experienced actress. However, the real highlight goes to Roberto Mallet's performance. He is an acting teacher (research his work, he follows the school of Master Constantin Stanislavski), and in this film, he clearly proved that he deeply understands what he teaches. I would say that a significant part of this film's probable success can be credited to him.

The film was very well written by Elton Mesquita. The verisimilitude of Catholicism, in relation to spiritual combat, was excellent, despite the fact that all art has a sort of poetic license that allows adaptations to make the film more believable, especially for those who enjoy the "God of Chance." I missed more locations that would show this "deep Brazil"-that Catholic Brazil of the past century, for example, with its baroque architecture. However, I understand that this absence is also due to the financial issue I mentioned initially.

It is a competent film! I hope to see Brazilian films reaching an increasingly higher level.
